terms.brief: Python/PyTorch environment the engine needs
terms.detail: Python compute stack (including PyTorch) used by the voice engine. Not in the installer; the first launch downloads the build for your GPU.

terms.brief: Shared model that turns audio into content features
terms.detail: HuBERT extracts what you said so the voice model can re-voice it. One global file for all voices; without it no voice works.

terms.brief: Pretrained base required to train a custom voice
terms.detail: Official pretrained acoustic bases. Training from them is much faster than from scratch; pick 32k / 40k / 48k to match your training sample rate.

terms.brief: Optional .index feature file for closer tone match
terms.detail: Stores training-audio features for closer tone. Optional; conversion works without it. Strength is “Index rate” in Settings.

terms.brief: GPU path for AMD/iGPU — convert yes, train no
terms.detail: Windows GPU acceleration for non-NVIDIA cards. Missing some ops needed for training, so training still needs NVIDIA.

terms.brief: NVIDIA-only inference speedup; falls back if unsupported
terms.detail: Pre-records GPU work to cut CPU↔GPU overhead, often lowering latency and VRAM. NVIDIA only; auto-falls back when unsupported.

terms.brief: rmvpe / harvest / pm / fcpe / crepe — rmvpe by default
terms.detail: How pitch is tracked. RMVPE is usually best and fastest; Harvest more stable but slower; PM fastest but fragile; FCPE/Crepe optional high-accuracy modes.

terms.brief: Timbre thickness; labeled “Formant” in the dock
terms.detail: Controls how thick or thin the voice sounds without changing pitch. Tune with pitch to match a character.

terms.brief: Input gate: quieter than this counts as silence
terms.detail: Levels below this (keyboard, fan, etc.) are treated as silence and not converted. When you speak, the dock meter should clearly cross the line.

terms.brief: How much output loudness follows your mic vs the voice model
terms.detail: Lower keeps the trained voice’s dynamics; higher keeps more of your speech dynamics.

terms.brief: How adjacent audio blocks are joined
terms.detail: Alternate crossfade join. Helps some voices, no change on others — A/B listen and decide.

terms.brief: Samples per second (often 32k / 40k / 48k)
terms.detail: Usually follow the device, or follow the voice model. Prefer “follow device” if unsure.

terms.brief: Classic Windows audio API — most compatible
terms.detail: Oldest Windows path; works with almost everything, higher latency. Default if unsure. Restart conversion after change.

terms.brief: Lower latency than MME, pickier devices
terms.detail: Newer Windows path with lower latency; some cards fail — switch back to MME. Exclusive mode is lower latency but locks the device.

terms.brief: Pro-audio low-latency path when a driver is installed
terms.detail: Lowest latency for pro interfaces (or ASIO4ALL). Only listed if a driver exists. One app at a time.

terms.brief: Hear the converted voice yourself
terms.detail: By default only games/chat hear conversion. Monitor plays a copy to your headphones — use a real device, not a virtual cable.

terms.brief: Audio chunk length: shorter is faster and heavier
terms.detail: Shorter blocks lower latency but cost more GPU; too short stutters. Restart conversion after change.

terms.brief: Overlap between adjacent blocks
terms.detail: Softens joins. Too short clicks; too long blurs. Defaults are fine.

terms.brief: Evens out loud and quiet speech
terms.detail: Pulls loud peaks down for steadier level. Too much sounds dull.

terms.brief: Band-level tone shaping
terms.detail: Boost or cut low/mid/high. Use presets if unsure.

terms.brief: Virtual audio line between this app and games (VB-Cable)
terms.detail: This app outputs to CABLE Input; games/chat use CABLE Output as mic. Reboot after install so devices appear.

terms.brief: Voice conversion stack this app uses
terms.detail: Retrieval-based Voice Conversion: each voice is its own model file; switching voices switches models.
